payload.rationale: The contract requires the 2026 GISS LOTI annual value to exceed both the 2025 value (1.19 C, comfortably cleared) and 1.28 C, so the binding threshold is 1.28 C (effectively a reported value of 1.29 C or higher). Supplied Jan–Aug 2026 anomalies average about 1.22 C (sum 9.79). To reach a reported 1.29, Sep–Dec must average roughly 1.41 C; to merely tie 1.28 they must average about 1.38 C. The August value of 1.40 C, a sharp jump from 1.25, suggests upward momentum (consistent with a developing warm ENSO phase, though no ENSO forecast is supplied), and late-year anomalies persisting near or above August levels are plausible given strong month-to-month autocorrelation. Historical analogs: in 2023 (El Niño onset) Sep–Dec GISS anomalies averaged ~1.4 C, which would suffice; in 2024 they averaged ~1.3 C, which would not. The outcome hinges on whether late-2026 months climb further from 1.40 rather than plateau, and on rounding to two decimals. Reasons this could be too high: one warm month may be noise; a plateau near 1.35 yields an annual ~1.27, failing; strict 'above 1.28' plus rounding removes near-misses; ENSO state is unknown. Reasons this could be too low: if El Niño is intensifying, Sep–Dec could exceed 1.45 (2023-like), making the threshold easy; September (already partly observed by the cutoff) may already be warm; GISS revisions could nudge values up. Overall I place the chance somewhat below even, around 30%.
limitations: No ENSO forecast, September partial data, or fitted predictive distribution for annual temperature supplied.
Threshold sensitivity: outcome likely decided by ~0.02 C, within monthly noise and revision/rounding uncertainty.
GISS data revisions between now and settlement could alter reported annual value.
Analog-based reasoning from a small number of past years.
